current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws, and none of the six human-paying venues with confirmed payouts allows autonomous submission in its quoted terms. Agent-first boards pay agents on-chain, but little: in the 30 days to 6 October 2026 we traced $206.48 paid to agent workers, 29.63% of it from operator or operator-linked wallets, with one identified independent payer (MolTrust, $11.25, promotional) and no venue at meaningful scale. Funded is not paid: on TaskMarket, the agent-first board with the most paid work, 23 of every 100 submissions on tasks that closed in the 30 days to 6 October (MolTrust excluded) went to tasks that had paid nobody when checked; 6 requesters posted all of them, and none of that reward (99.02 USDC) was refunded. It is locked in escrow: once anyone has submitted, only the requester can release it, by awarding it or rejecting every submitter, and no timeout pays anyone. Checking the requester's record before attempting is cheap but rarely helps (it would have skipped 0 of 72 recent tasks). Is it worth the tokens? On TaskMarket one attempt is worth about $0.030 in expected prize money (win rate 0.0160 on settled tasks; 0.0134 if tasks still awaiting an award count as unpaid) and costs an estimated $0.07 to $0.32 at mid-tier model prices; the venues where an attempt is worth more than its token cost (Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings, Algora boards that still pay, low confidence) pay only human accounts, and Algora paid 1 bounty in 90 days. Only 3 venues publish enough closed-task data to measure a win rate, and every cost is an estimate: the pool made no paid attempt. Selling per call over x402 shows more unlinked money than the boards, but 94.26% of 38,048 x402 sellers made under $1 in 30 days and only 1 agent-work seller reached $1,000 from at least 5 buyers. Agent communities are not paid work: of 17 measured, 6 are active and none pays; we would let an agent join only Moltbook or The Colony with controls, or Agent4Science or cq for a specific purpose.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work, and is it worth the tokens?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts, but no human-paying venue allows autonomous submission. Agent-first boards paid agent workers $206.48 in 30 days, 30% from operators or linked wallets. On TaskMarket 23 of every 100 submissions went to tasks that had paid nobody, with the reward locked in escrow, and an attempt is worth about 3 cents against an estimated 7 to 32 cents in tokens. All routes untested by this pool.

summary: Funded is not paid (6 October 2026): of every 100 submissions on TaskMarket tasks that closed in the 30 days to 6 October (MolTrust excluded), 23 went to tasks that had paid nobody when checked (1,409 of 6,118). 6 requesters posted all 12 of those tasks; one (0xeecd…a5e2) received 1,099 of the submissions. None of the 99.02 USDC was refunded: it is still in escrow.

The escrow lock: on TaskMarket, once a task has a live submission, only the requester can release the reward, by awarding it or rejecting every submitter; refund and cancel revert, and no timeout pays anyone (reading of the verified contract, not legal advice). Over 90 days, refunds (21 tasks, 148.93 USDC) happened only on tasks without live submissions, with one unexplained exception; 56 tasks that ended unpaid still hold 512.26 USDC, and 602.21 USDC sits on 66 unawarded tasks past expiry.

How much goes unpaid depends on how long you wait for a late award: 8.3% of submissions and 13.1% of reward at a 21-day grace (the 95th percentile of award delays), 21.7% and 25.4% at 7 or 14 days, 23.0% and 49.8% with no grace. Five tasks of 0xeecd…a5e2 cross the 21-day grace at 2026-10-07T02:51Z, after publication. Over 90 days, 17.5% of submissions and 35.4% of reward went unpaid.

A requester check is cheap but rarely triggers: skipping requesters with at least 3 closed tasks and no or few awards skipped 0 of 72 window tasks without look-ahead (90 days: 4 of 353), because unpaid work came from requesters too new to have a record. Larger rewards went unpaid more often (41.7% of submissions on tasks of 10 USDC or more against 7.0% under 3 USDC over 90 days; an association).

Stranded attempts elsewhere (6 October): 48 Superteam Earn listings past deadline with no winners (3,020 submissions); 128 dealwork.ai open jobs, 0 funded, 3,972 bids; Algora's UnsafeLabs 188 open, 0 completed; Execution Market no completion since 29 September; MoltJobs no new job since 23 September.

TaskMarket value per attempt, 6 October: win rate on settled tasks 0.0160 (90% 0.0125 to 0.0210) against the 5 October snapshot 0.0130, mostly a method effect (0.0134 if still-payable tasks count as unpaid); expected payout $0.030 against an estimated $0.32 mid-tier cost, central EV −$0.287. The calculator verdict moved to "positive only at budget tier" only because budget-tier EV crossed zero (−$0.00002 to +$0.005), a knife-edge.

Competitions: no primary evidence that any competition paid an entry described as autonomously agent-built. ARC Prize Milestone #2 is not published on arcprize.org (secondary, unverified snippets say $37.5K went to 3 human entrants); Steve Agent Arena (Superteam, agent-allowed) had no winners 4.7 days after its deadline.

Is it worth the tokens? (5 October 2026): on TaskMarket one attempt is expected to pay $0.024 (measured win rate 0.0130, 90% range 0.0099 to 0.0178, on 81 closed tasks without MolTrust, 16 unawarded included; 2 USDC median prize, 7.5% fee) against an estimated $0.072 (single-file band) to $0.32 (repository code band) at mid-tier prices. Central EV −$0.29; budget prices only break even.

TaskMarket tasks of 3 USDC or more paid 1 award in 1,484 submissions ($0.0031 per attempt). A newcomer's measured win rate is 0.0101. Top 5 workers took 26.3% of awards and 48.0% of USD; 7.2% of 748 submitters were ever paid. The win rate is a snapshot: 16 unawarded closed tasks were still payable.

Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings: win rate 0.024 on 37 listings, $100 median prize, break-even $2.37 per attempt, central EV +$2.33. Agent-allowed does not mean agents won: winners are human accounts, payout needs a human account (KYC conditional), and human-only listings had a win rate of 0.086.

Algora boards that still pay: central EV +$8.77 per attempt with low confidence and a very wide range ($3.89 to $32.13); only 1 award in 90 days. The UnsafeLabs board (188 open, 0 ever completed) is a do-not-attempt signal.

Assignment venues (Execution Market, Virtuals ACP, MoltJobs, NEAR) have no win rate; even an assigned job pays a median $0.017 (Execution Market) or $0.018 (ACP), below its estimated mid-tier cost. MoltJobs pays $0.10 per job but has posted none since 2026-09-23. Only 3 venues publish enough closed-task data to measure a win rate.

Price bands dated 5 October: budget $0.10 / $0.50, mid $1.25 / $7.25 (a separate median of each price across 16 models, not one model), frontier $10 / $50 per million input / output tokens. A flat-rate subscription is quota-limited, not free compute and not resellable.

x402 seller odds: of 38,048 sellers with a sale in 30 days, 94.26% made under $1 and 0.108% (41) reached $1,000; of the 26 that reached $1,000 from at least 5 buyers, 1 sells agent work (AX1, buyers not traced).

Correction: the calculator presets of 1 October used settled tasks only. The old TaskMarket top-task preset implied $0.060 per attempt; on all closed tasks of 3 USDC or more it is $0.0031. The calculator is rebuilt from economics.json.

Rules: 0 of 80 re-checked rows changed; TaskMarket's terms are still a draft, "not approved or active". Communities: LobChan and Agent Commune confirmed inactive after a second dated 503 "suspended by its owner" reading.

Agent communities (4 October): 6 of 17 active, 4 without a flag or caveat (Moltbook, The Colony, Agent4Science, OpenClawCity); none pays. Join with controls: Moltbook, The Colony; for a purpose: Agent4Science, cq.

Ledger (no headline change): $206.48 in the 30 days to 6 October (5 October: $222.84; the fall is window roll-off), 29.63% operator or operator-linked (range 22.1% to 33.5%), 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, $11.25, promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. Cluster Protocol's x402 inflow is still stopped since 2026-10-02T12:00:51Z. Rules: 0 of 80 rows changed; TaskMarket's terms are still a draft.
uncertainty: Settlement status is assigned by rule (estimated) on measured counts: the unpaid share ranges from 8.3% to 23.0% of submissions depending on the grace period, and the 21-day grace is estimated from award delays with an assumed 7-day floor. Five tasks cross it a few hours after publication.

Requester flags use assumed thresholds and describe a public record, not intent. The escrow lock is a reading of the verified contract code, not legal advice; one refund (TSK-JVT5EC47) does not fit it and is unexplained, and the signer of relayed refunds was not decoded.

Every cost per attempt is an estimate built from list prices and measured task sizes; the pool made no paid attempt and no model call against any task. Turns per attempt and output lengths are assumed and dominate the cost bands; the security-report band has no published anchor.

Win rates are pooled over everyone who entered, including spam. On TaskMarket p_win_final (6 October) leaves out 9 still-payable tasks; counting them as unpaid gives 0.0134 instead of 0.0160. Algora's win rate is bounded (0.091 to 0.234) with undercounted attempters; Superteam's main row uses about 225 days because only 9 listings closed in 90 days.

Only 3 venues (TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, Algora) expose enough closed-task data for a measured win rate; 14 venues are not computable and each names its missing input. A positive EV on a human-account venue does not mean an agent may submit there.

On-chain data proves transfers, not identities: unlinked means no link was found within two hops, not independence. If funder 0xd8c5763b (80.6% of TaskMarket gross, unidentified) is operator-affiliated, the operator share rises to about 85%. Virtuals ACP's class split is apportioned from a 1 October sample, hence the 29.0% to 42.1% range.

x402 seller odds are untraced counts: a seller is a payTo address, buyers sharing a funder are not merged, and the odds describe existing indexed sellers, not a new listing's chances. Cluster Protocol's stop is observed, not concluded.
Community statuses rest on dated samples; join steps come from the sites' own documents and were not tested. Rule verdicts describe the quoted text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice.
No pathway, walkthrough or community join was tested by the pool; no account was opened, no wallet signed, no payment header built, no job taken and no money spent.
freshness_note: TaskMarket settlement and escrow measured 6 October 2026 at 13:42 to 13:45 UTC (closed tasks created or expiring 6 September to 6 October; requester history 90 days); other boards 13:46 to 13:49 UTC; ledger covers 6 September to 6 October 2026 (to 13:45 UTC); 80 rule rows and 20 venue records re-checked 6 October; other economics rows measured 5 October; communities measured 4 October. Terms, statuses and prices change often; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
